Vision & Values
We are a state primary school in the grounds of the beautiful Braywick Nature Reserve in Bray, Berkshire. We offer a small, safe and nurturing environment which gives children the opportunity to thrive and succeed with confidence. Every pupil is valued as an individual, and known personally by every member of our staff.
Our experienced teaching staff consistently provide our pupils with exciting and engaging learning opportunities, inspiring them to achieve to the best of their ability. Our children are all encouraged to be best they can be, to aspire to fulfil their dreams and to succeed in all that they do. Braywick Court School pupils love coming to school and have a passion for learning.

Diary Dates

Attendance
Leave of absence
Amendments to the Education (Pupil |Registration) Regulations state that headteachers may not grant any leave of absence during term time unless there are exceptional circumstances. A family holiday is not classed as exceptional circumstances.
Illness upon return from abroad
Any child who has been unwell whilst abroad may not return to school until they are fully recovered. A doctor’s note explaining the illness and confirming recovery will be required.
Unauthorised absence
Long unauthorised absences are recorded on your child’s profile – to be passed on throughout his/her whole education. They also damage the school’s reputation as they are recorded as ‘truancy’ in the league table of schools published annually.
Sign below using your finger or mouse, upon completing the form, to show you have read and understood the above.

Extended care
We are proud to offer an extensive extended care programme exclusively for our pupils. Managed and delivered by staff who are also part of our main school team, this ensures that the high standards of our provision are consistent throughout each child's experience with us.
We are committed to educating the whole child, and our extended care programme is thoughtfully designed to enhance, extend, and enrich the high-quality curriculum offered during the school day.
We encourage as many children as possible to participate in the wide range of activities available, as this forms an integral part of the overall Braywick Court School experience. Our goal is for every child to engage in extended care in some way. To support this, we offer funded places in certain sessions for children entitled to Pupil Premium.
Timings
Active Start: 8.00-8.40am
After-school clubs: 3:15pm-4:15pm every day
Evening Owls: 4:15pm-5:30pm (5pm on a Friday)
Active Start
Active Start runs every day from 8:00-8:40am. This is the perfect way to start the day and get energised ready for learning. It is a fun and energising activity led by our specialist sports coach. Our pupils have the opportunity to take part in a range of activities including team games, new sports and morning workouts.
After School Clubs
We currently offer over 20 after school clubs per week, coordinated by our Extended Care Manager, Miss Sarah Feely. After-school clubs run for 3:15pm-4:15pm every day. Our clubs change termly and are available for all pupils. Recent activities on offer include:
Athletics
Arts & Crafts
Badminton
Bikeability (cycle training)
Book Club
Cricket
Chill Club
Coding
Dance
Dodgeball
Football
Film Club
Funky Fingers
Gymnastics
Homework
Nature Explorers
Photography
Pillo Polo
Story STEM
11+ Tuition
Evening Owls
Evening Owls offers a home away from home setting where children can have unstructured play in a relaxed environment. Evening Owls runs from 4:15pm -5:30pm (5pm on a Friday).
During Evening Owls, children are able to select from a range of activities. There is also an opportunity for organised games, stories and arts and crafts. It is also a great opportunity for an adult to listen to the younger children read.
Parents have the option of ordering tea, which is served between 4:30pm-5pm.
Ad-Hoc Extended Care
If you require a one-off club for your child please contact the office to book a place. To note: Booking an ad hoc club will incur a £1 premium on standard club fees; a place will be offered in the club that has available space.
Holiday Club
We run regular holiday clubs for our pupils, but children can take advantage of our ‘Recommend a Friend’ offer and bring along a non-school pupil to play!
Holiday Club is planned around a theme and combines a mixture of active and focused activities throughout the day. It runs from 9.00am- 4:00pm.
If you would like to join our holiday club and are a friend of a pupil of the school please complete the attached form.
Fees and Payment Details
After School Clubs (until 4.15pm)
Evening Owls (Mon - Thursday until 5.30pm)
Evening owls (Friday until 5pm)
If you’d like to pay your outstanding balance using childcare vouchers, email the office with a copy of your transaction to clubs@braywickcourtschool.org.uk so that your account can be manually credited.
Pupil Premium: Children in receipt of PPG are entitled to one free after school club per term, and a 50% discount on Holiday Club. Your account will be amended by us to reflect one free club per term.
Timely payments: all fees are due in advance termly, before clubs and extended care starts. All previous club payments must be settled by end of term. Any outstanding payments after this date will result in your child not being assigned clubs until this is rectified.
Reinvesting funds
Our extended care programme is run by Braywick Court, for Braywick Court. This means that all funds generated from the program are reinvested directly into the school to benefit our students.
These funds help to support specialist music and Spanish teaching, as well as our sports coaches, which are key components of our extensive curriculum that goes beyond the national curriculum requirements. Additionally, the funds contribute to enhancements such as IT equipment and high-quality art and design technology resources.
If you have any questions or queries, do not hesitate to get in contact via email: pe@braywickcourtschool.org.uk

English: Writing, Reading & Oracy
At Braywick Court School, proficiency in reading, writing, and oracy is vital to the lifelong success of our pupils. We believe every child can become a fluent, thoughtful, and lifelong reader, as well as a confident, capable communicator whose words have the power to shape their future.
English knowledge and skills are taught through an integrated approach where oral rehearsal feeds writing, high-quality literature fuels composition, and rich discussion deepens comprehension.
Writing
At Braywick Court School, we don't just teach writing; we help children find their voice. Our vision is built on the simple truth that if a child cannot say it, they cannot write it. That’s why our classrooms are filled with talk, rehearsing sentences and debating vocabulary long before a pen touches paper.
We follow a clear, consistent writing journey.
From the first marks in EYFS to the polished, published pieces, we want our pupils to be proud of their craft. We aim for every child to leave us as a confident, capable communicator who knows that their words have the power to shape their future.
The Five PIllars of Writing
High-quality writing is impossible without high-quality reading
If a child cannot say it, they can’t write it.
If handwriting and spelling aren’t automatic the writing will stall.
High quality content and writing outcomes for a meaningful purpose.
A clear writing journey is embedded and followed.
Reading
At Braywick Court School, we don’t just teach children to read; we teach them to think, feel, and belong through reading. Reading must be taught deliberately, not left to chance. A child who reads fluently and with understanding can access the full curriculum and the wider world beyond it.
Our approach is built on three core truths:
If a child can decode, they can access the text.
If a child understands what they read, they are truly reading.
If a child enjoys reading, they will choose to read again and again.
Our classrooms are rich with stories, discussion, explicit vocabulary instruction, and purposeful reading. We make deliberate choices about the literature we share to broaden knowledge, reflect diverse experiences, and inspire a lifelong love of books. From early phonics to deep literary discussion, we aim for every pupil to leave Braywick Court School as a fluent reader, a thoughtful reader, and a lifelong reader.
The Five Pillars of Reading
Reading begins with secure foundations.
Fluent, automatic decoding unlocks access to meaning.
Reading is understanding.
Pupils construct meaning by connecting vocabulary, knowledge and ideas.
Reading is both a skill and a habit.
When children enjoy reading, they choose it, regularly and independently
Talk deepens understanding.
Through discussion, pupils clarify, justify and refine their thinking.
We teach pupils how to read, not just what to read.
High-quality texts are explored in depth so pupils learn how meaning is constructed.
Oracy
Our core principle for writing and thinking is simple: If a child cannot say it, they cannot write it. High-quality oracy education directly impacts academic outcomes, builds confidence, and equips pupils to express themselves articulately and creatively both in the classroom and beyond.
Oral Rehearsal: Pupils test, refine, and rehearse their ideas and sentences using structured stems before picking up a pen.
Active Dialogue: Staff foster an inclusive environment where all pupils actively participate in discussions, build on each other's ideas, and regularly practice verbalising their learning.
Performance & Public Speaking: Children are given a wealth of opportunities across the curriculum and wider school life to develop their spoken language. From reading their own drafts aloud to "hear" punctuation and flow, to performing poetry, presenting speeches, and taking part in dramatic productions, pupils build expression, tone, and confidence in speaking before an audience.
Phonics and Early Reading
Early reading is taught daily from Preschool to Year 2 through Monster Phonics, an award-winning, multi-sensory systematic synthetic phonics programme.
All staff are fully trained in this approach, which brings learning to life using colour-coded graphemes and engaging monster characters to represent long vowel sounds, silent letters, and tricky spellings.
By categorising the 44 English sounds into 10 monster-led groups and weaving in songs, games, and active practice, complex spelling patterns become memorable and fun. Daily whole-class lessons explicitly teach phoneme-grapheme correspondence, decoding, blending, segmenting, and reading for meaning.
To ensure pupils read with early confidence, the decodable books sent home are strictly matched to the phonic sounds mastered in class. By Year 2, the programme seamlessly incorporates national curriculum spelling and grammar rules, ensuring pupils transition smoothly into Key Stage 2 equipped with strong decoding automaticity and a genuine love for reading.
Decodable Reading Books
We have Monster Phonics books available in school and they are used during guided reading sessions and as take home books. The Monster Phonics books are fully decodable. This means that children can read them using just their phonics skills and knowledge.
The sounds in the book that children take home reflect the sequence of sounds taught in school meaning that your child should be able to read this text at around 90% accuracy and fluency. It is important that pupils are given the opportunity to re-read books many times to build up their fluency and confidence in word reading. Pupils also have access to the eBook library of previously read Monster Phonics books.
Assessment of Phonics and Early Reading
Regular and efficient monitoring of children’s development in phonics is essential if they are to become competent and confident readers, and subsequently writers. The Monster Phonics programme has a clearly mapped set of assessments which allows for checking children’s grapheme-phoneme correspondence (GPC), knowledge of High-Frequency Words (HFWs) and Common Exception Words (CEWs) for reading and writing.
The assessment schedule for Monster Phonics is broken down for each year group; Reception, Year One and Year Two. Each year group has a set of graphemes, CEWs and HFWs to be learnt and then assessed.
Pupils in Year 1 are well prepared for the Phonics Screening Check which takes place in the Summer Term.
Find out more about Monster Phonics
An Introduction to Monster Phonics
Supporting Your Child with Monster Phonics
Monster Phonics Tips for Parents
Year 3 to Year 6 - Reading
All children who attend Braywick Court School to leave us fully literate and with a life long love of books and reading.
Once our pupils have moved beyond phonics and early reading, they are explicitly taught through daily whole class reading lessons. Pupils from Year 2 to Year 6 have a dedicated 30 minute whole class reading lesson every day following the Master Readers approach.
Core texts have been chosen to complement the topics pupils are studying within the wider curriculum and also link to pupils writing in English lessons.
To further develop a love of reading, all teachers promote reading for pleasure by reading to their class every day.
Pupils in Key Stage 2 (from Year 3-6) follow the Oxford Reading Tree reading levels and have access to a wide range of genres of reading material, as well as the class and school libraries.

Foreign Languages
We value the study of modern foreign languages (MFL) and therefore all children begin learning Spanish from the age of 2 years old at our preschool. We teach Spanish during curriculum time across the school, with additional languages offered through our After School Club provision.
Bilinguasing have been providing high quality MFL for us since we opened in 2014. Specialist teachers make learning fun and extend the children well beyond the requirement of the national curriculum.

Personal, Social, Health & Citizenship Education
At Braywick Court School, PSHCE is woven into the heart of everything we do. We believe that when children understand themselves and the world around them, they grow into confident, independent, reflective, and responsible members of an ever changing society.
Our PSHCE curriculum aims to nurture learners who are articulate, resilient, and confident to share their views and opinions. We provide a safe, nurturing environment where pupils are challenged intellectually, socially, spiritually, and morally.
Through progressive, age appropriate learning across PSHCE & RSE education, we ensure every child receives clear, accurate, and balanced guidance. Pupils learn how to build healthy, respectful relationships, navigate the online and offline worlds safely, manage their physical and mental wellbeing, and make informed, thoughtful choices regarding money and their futures.
By recognising their unique self worth and strengths, Braywick Court School children are empowered to navigate life opportunities and challenges, play a positive role in school life and the wider community, and grow into happy, active global citizens.
PSHCE Curriculum
PSHCE & RSE is taught weekly throughout the school, following the Kapow Primary schemes of work as a guide.
At Braywick Court, the impact of our PSHCE & RSE curriculum extends far beyond the classroom walls and goes deeperthan simple recall of knowledge. When taught consistently through a well sequenced curriculum, PSHCE & RSE transforms how our children interact, make choices, and navigate everyday situations.
Learning is embedded through dedicated PSHCE & RSE lessons, core value assemblies, and whole school participation in national events such as Safer Internet Day, Anti Bullying Week, and Mental Health Awareness Month. Through interactive methods such as drama, circle time, and reflective discussion, pupils develop self awareness, emotional literacy, and strong communication skills.
Our pupils leave Braywick Court School equipped with the agency, moral compass, and emotional maturity needed to thrive as happy, responsible members of society.
Personal Development
At Braywick Court School, PSHCE is the foundation for a rich personal development offer that nurtures the whole child. We actively build character and cultural capital by extending learning beyond the classroom into every aspect of school life.
Through meaningful pupil leadership opportunities, our inclusive house system, purposeful curriculum enrichment, and active community engagement, children gain real world experience in active citizenship.
These shared experiences foster a deep sense of belonging, encourage pupils to articulate their views, and empower them to make a positive contribution to both our school and the wider community.

As part of the Bellevue Place Education Trust, our school has the chance to participate in numerous annual trust-wide competitions. These provide our pupils the opportunity to collaborate with students from other schools, build teamwork, develop resilience, and hone their talents in a variety of areas.
Competitions we offer include:
Sport Competition
As an active member of the Ascot & Maidenhead Schools Sports Partnership (AMSSP), we strive to give every child the opportunity to represent the school in a sporting activity at least once.
Children are given the chance to participate in a range of activities, including introductory workshops, enrichment tournaments, and competitive fixtures. In addition to the AMSSP, we also take part in trust-wide tournaments and competitive sports with schools in the BPET Berkshire Hub.

Music
Our music curriculum is developed to nurture and enhance the individuality of each child. Music gives our pupils a link between school and the world around them, bringing our community together though shared experiences. Music should spark a child’s imagination, providing them with opportunities to explore and challenges to tackle. Music at Braywick Court ignites a life time of passion for every child.
Our music curriculum exposes our pupils to a wide range of genres, styles and musicians, this ensures that they have a culturally rich musical knowledge. Children develop skills in responding to music, playing and performing, singing, improvising and composing. Pupils also have shared experiences of listening and responding to music, and the opportunity to pursue individual passions through learning an instrument of their choice.
Scheme of work
Our carefully mapped curriculum follows the Charanga scheme, ensuring that all staff can confidently deliver high quality music teaching. Pupils have the opportunity to perform to an audience, celebrating their musical talent. We work closely with Berkshire Maestros to offer a wide range of individual instrumental tuition and strongly encourage our pupils to learn to play an instrument.
Music education is part of every child’s world of possibility, regardless of their background or starting point. We offer further musical enrichment through our extra curricular activities as well as through annual projects such as In2Music.
I would teach children music, for the patterns of music and all the arts are the keys of learning.

pageCache.pageTitle: Braywick Court School - Home Learning & Remote Education
pageCache.text:
Home Learning and Remote Education
Our priority is to deliver face-to-face, high-quality education to all pupils.
The evidence is clear that being out of education causes significant harm to educational attainment, life chances, mental and physical health. We are, therefore, committed to deliver a balanced and high-quality curricular provision to all pupils, including during temporary school closures.
In the event of a school closure of any duration, we will offer immediate remote education to families with continuation of the high standards of learning that characterise the normal school day.
Emergency School Closure
In the event of very bad weather or other force majeure situations, the decision to close the school will be taken after great consideration. We will only close the school if it is absolutely necessary.
In the event of any school closure at short notice we will contact all parents via email and will post a message on our school Facebook page.
Remote learning will be set by teaching staff via our online platforms: Google Classroom, Century Tech, Monster Phonics, TT Rockstars and Numbots.
Home Learning
Learning at home is an essential part of good education. Regular home learning is important, since it gives pupils the opportunity to practise at home tasks done in the class, and helps the pupils work towards improving important skills. It also helps children to become confident and independent in their learning, which will help throughout their time at school, and in adult life.
Home learning is categorised as any activity that pupils undertake outside of timetabled lesson time.
Our home learning policy clearly outline expectations for parents regarding supporting learning at home:
Home Learning Policy

Trips and Residentials
Educational trips and residentials provide safe opportunities for children to learn outside the classroom, develop important life skills, and they bring their classroom learning to life. These experiences are designed to complement the curriculum and enhance the children's learning in a fun and engaging way.
We understand the importance of caregivers and parental involvement in our trips and residentials, so we provide detailed information about each trip, including the itinerary, activities, and safety measures in place.
Day Visits
Day visits are one of many ways for children to gain knowledge on topics taught in our curriculum, while engaging with their local community. We provide a range of day visits to pupils which enhance and enrich their learning.

Residentials
A residential trip is an important milestone in a child’s life, playing a key role in developing their confidence and independence. These trips are an integral part of each pupil’s personal development, offering valuable experiences that help prepare them for secondary school.
Year 4 pupils have the opportunity to visit Ufton Court on a two-day residential trip, immersing themselves in the world of the Anglo Saxons and Vikings. The children get to experience a range of practical activities, role play and a costume banquet!
Year 6 visit Manor Adventure in Shropshire. Staying at the 100 acre site for five days, they have the chance to explore a range of outdoor adventure pursuits. This trip is the perfect springboard for the pupil’s transition to secondary school.

Preschool curriculum
We follow the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) curriculum that sets standards for learning, development and care of children from birth to 5 years old. The framework supports an integrated approach to early learning and care. It gives us principles to deliver quality early education and childcare experiences for all children.
The EYFS curriculum includes seven areas of learning and development:
Children who attend Braywick Court Preschool get the very best start to their education and are exceptionally well prepared for the transition to primary school. Children who join our primary school having attended our preschool have a smooth and seamless transition with consistency of their learning environment, curriculum, staffing and teaching style.

Preschool to primary school transition
If you are considering applying for a Reception place at Braywick Court School, we would strongly recommend that you enrol them at our preschool in order to have continuity in their learning journey: our curriculum has been thought right from our preschool to Year 6, as highlighted by the latest Ofsted report.
It is important to know that if your child attends our preschool, this does not necessarily qualify them to a place at our primary school (places are administered by the the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead).

Personal Development
We are dedicated to developing children into confident, all-rounded individuals, excelling both academically and personally. Braywick Court School places a high value on the important job it does to influence and enhance every element of a child’s life, going beyond academic success.
Pupil Leadership
Leadership roles and responsibilities are offered to pupils of all ages and are democratically elected. Through taking on these roles pupils are given the opportunity to be active citizens within our school community, positively contributing to the life of the school. Pupils know that they have a voice and can affect meaningful change within school.
Here are a few examples of leadership roles on offer:
House Captain
School Council
Play Leader
Sports Leader
Reading Champion
Librarian.
Community Engagement
We live and breathe the motto ‘It takes a village to raise a child’ and as such, pupils are encouraged to participate in a variety of community events to enhance their understanding of collaboration and community cohesion. The school council and PTA regularly organise fundraising events, such as supporting a local charitable cause.
Additionally, pupils are motivated to contribute positively to their local community through activities like donating to the food bank, participating in the Thames Hospice sponsored run, and taking part in the Bray Village Remembrance service.
Above and Beyond the National Curriculum
Braywick Court pupils are exceptionally well-prepared for the next stage in their learning and for the wider world. We are committed to ensuring that our pupils become global citizens who aspire to make a positive impact on the world.
Pupils are provided with opportunities to explore real-world applications of their learning, helping them understand how theory is put into practice and broadening their perspective on the wider world.
Enrichment activities, such as Year 6 Enterprise, educational visits, and guest speakers, expand our pupils' understanding of the world of work and inspire them to strive for an ambitious future.

Diversity & Inclusion
We are committed to ensuring equality of opportunity for all pupils, staff, parents, and carers, regardless of race, gender, disability, belief, sexual orientation, age, or socio-economic background.
We strive to foster a culture of inclusion and diversity where everyone connected to the school feels proud of their identity and empowered to participate fully in school life. Our goal is to promote respect for differences and celebrate diversity in alignment with our core school values.

SEND Information & Documents
We work within the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead guidance on provision for children with SEND in mainstream schools, which explains the ways pupils with different additional needs are provided for within the school. We also follow our ‘Equality and Disability’ policy and we also have an ‘Accessibility Strategy and Action Plan.
We are dedicated to fostering an inclusive ethos throughout our school community. We believe that inclusion is closely linked to diversity and equality, which we actively promote for all children in our care, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, impairment, achievement, or background. We are committed to providing adaptive support and ensuring the high achievement of all learner groups.
Our Goals
We adhere to the Royal Borough of Windsor and Maidenhead's guidance on provision for children with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND). Our school maintains strong partnerships with external agencies that offer additional advice and support. We also have access to advisory teachers and educational psychologists employed by the local authority.
SEND and Inclusion Team
Our Inclusion Manager is Mrs Louise Dembowicz who is responsible for overseeing the Special Education Needs and Disability Policy, and coordinating the specific provision which supports individual children with SEND. Our SENCo works closely with pupils, staff, parents and external specialist agencies to ensure the needs of all SEND pupils are met.
Our SENCo coordinates specific provisions to support children with SEND and mental health challenges. She collaborates closely with pupils, staff, parents, and external specialists to ensure that the needs of all SEND pupils are met.
You can contact our Inclusion Team through the school office by calling 01628 782 562 or emailing office@braywickcourtschool.org.uk
Please note our SENCo working days are: Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday

Art & Design
Arts subjects provide a plethora of benefits, such as helping pupils build a sense of identity, enabling them to make sense of the world, as well as having a profoundly positive impact on well-being and mental health.
Our aim during the Create term is to develop pupils’ knowledge and skills in art and design through an inquiry-based approach. Each year group looks at a range of artists and craft-makers, building an artistic vocabulary as pupils move up the school, in order to respond to their works in a variety of ways, such as drama, music and literature as well as art.
With a whole term dedicated to Create, we are able to explore each technique and artist in depth, and give the pupils agency when it comes to their learning. As well as building artistic skills, pupils will have a wealth of opportunities to research, express themselves and develop their communication skills.

Computing
At Braywick Court School, our Computing curriculum inspires pupils to become curious, adaptable, and analytical digital thinkers who view technology through the lens of critical innovation. Operating as a Google School, we seamlessly blend explicit computing instruction with practical daily application across our wider curriculum.
We deliver the National Curriculum using the Kapow Primary Curriculum, covering dedicated core units per year alongside targeted enhanced 'Online Safety' units. Rather than treating computing as an isolated skill, technology is an active driver across all disciplines.
With 1-to-1 device access (Chromebooks) for all pupils across Key Stage 2, technology is integrated throughout the curriculum, whether children are conducting scientific research, designing historical presentations, creating reports, collating data, compiling biographies or producing digital art and music compositions.Our curriculum systematically maps learning across three core computing strands:
Computer Science: Understanding digital systems, networks, algorithms, physical computing, and programming languages (from block code to Python).
Information Technology: Utilising digital tools, spreadsheets, databases, and Google Workspace purposefully to store, manipulate, and present media.
Digital Literacy: Navigating the online world safely, critically, and responsibly while building a positive digital footprint.
Integrated Technology & Digital Excellence
At Braywick Court School, technology is not an isolated subject; it is woven into the culture of our school and the daily delivery of our curriculum. Aligned with the BPET Digital Strategy, we utilise technology through the lens of the SAMR pedagogical framework, ensuring digital tools are not merely substituted for paper, but are used to transform, enrich, and enhance learning across all subjects. Our classrooms are models of highly effective practice for the seamless integration of technoloy to enhance teaching and learning.
The Five Pillars of Computing
Our curriculum intentionally exceeds statutory National Curriculum expectations to deliver enhanced technical fluency, critical citizenship, and secondary readiness.
